questions.text: How many pillars of Islam are there?
questions.arabicText: كم عدد أركان الإسلام؟
questions.explanation: The Five Pillars are: Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm, and Hajj.

questions.text: How many times a day do Muslims pray?
questions.arabicText: كم مرة يصلي المسلمون في اليوم؟
questions.explanation: Muslims pray Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha — five times daily.

questions.text: What is the first surah of the Quran?
questions.arabicText: ما هي أول سورة في القرآن الكريم؟
questions.explanation: Al-Fatiha (The Opening) is the first surah and is recited in every unit of prayer.

questions.text: Who was the last Prophet of Islam?
questions.arabicText: من هو آخر نبي في الإسلام؟
questions.explanation: Prophet Muhammad (SAW) is the seal of all prophets and the last messenger of Allah.

questions.text: In which month do Muslims fast?
questions.arabicText: في أي شهر يصوم المسلمون؟
questions.explanation: Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar and the month of obligatory fasting.

questions.text: What is the holy book of Islam?
questions.arabicText: ما هو الكتاب المقدس في الإسلام؟
questions.explanation: The Quran is the final revelation from Allah, revealed to Prophet Muhammad (SAW).

questions.text: What does "Islam" mean in Arabic?
questions.arabicText: ماذا تعني كلمة "إسلام" باللغة العربية؟
questions.explanation: Islam means "submission to the will of Allah." It shares its root with "salam" (peace).

questions.text: In which city was the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) born?
questions.arabicText: في أي مدينة وُلد النبي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم؟
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) was born in Makkah (Mecca) in the Year of the Elephant, 570 CE.

questions.text: How many surahs are in the Quran?
questions.arabicText: كم عدد سور القرآن الكريم؟
questions.explanation: The Quran contains 114 surahs (chapters), starting with Al-Fatiha and ending with An-Nas.

questions.text: What is the direction Muslims face when praying?
questions.arabicText: ما هو الاتجاه الذي يواجهه المسلمون أثناء الصلاة؟
questions.explanation: Muslims face the Kaaba in Makkah — this direction is called the Qibla.

questions.text: Which angel is responsible for delivering revelation?
questions.arabicText: أي ملاك مسؤول عن تبليغ الوحي؟
questions.explanation: Angel Jibreel (Gabriel) delivered the revelations of the Quran to Prophet Muhammad (SAW).

questions.text: What is the minimum amount of Zakat payable (Nisab in gold terms)?
questions.explanation: The Nisab threshold for gold is 85 grams. Zakat is 2.5% of wealth held for one lunar year.

questions.text: In which year did the Hijra (migration to Madinah) take place?
questions.explanation: The Hijra took place in 622 CE. This event marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar.

questions.text: Which surah is known as the "Heart of the Quran"?
questions.arabicText: أي سورة تُعرف بـ"قلب القرآن"؟
questions.explanation: Surah Yasin (Chapter 36) is referred to as the heart of the Quran in several hadith.

questions.text: How many rakats are in the Fajr (dawn) prayer?
questions.arabicText: كم عدد ركعات صلاة الفجر؟
questions.explanation: Fajr prayer consists of 2 obligatory (fard) rakats. It is prayed between dawn and sunrise.

questions.text: What does "Inshallah" mean?
questions.arabicText: ماذا تعني "إن شاء الله"؟
questions.explanation: "Inshallah" (إن شاء الله) means "If Allah wills." Muslims say it when referring to future events.

questions.text: Which Prophet is known as Khalilullah (Friend of Allah)?
questions.arabicText: أي نبي يُعرف بخليل الله؟
questions.explanation: Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) AS was given the title Khalilullah — the intimate friend of Allah.

questions.text: What is the name of the night journey of the Prophet (SAW)?
questions.arabicText: ما اسم رحلة الإسراء والمعراج للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم؟
questions.explanation: Al-Isra wal Miraj — the night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem and ascension to the heavens.

questions.text: Which surah contains Ayat al-Kursi (the Throne Verse)?
questions.arabicText: أي سورة تحتوي على آية الكرسي؟
questions.explanation: Ayat al-Kursi is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah. It is the greatest verse in the Quran.

questions.text: What is the name of the well in Makkah associated with Hajar (AS)?
questions.arabicText: ما اسم البئر في مكة المرتبطة بهاجر عليها السلام؟
questions.explanation: The Zamzam well miraculously appeared for Hajar and her son Ismail (AS). It still flows today.

questions.text: How many Prophets are mentioned by name in the Quran?
questions.explanation: 25 Prophets are mentioned by name in the Quran, from Adam (AS) to Muhammad (SAW).

questions.text: What is the longest surah in the Quran?
questions.arabicText: ما هي أطول سورة في القرآن الكريم؟
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Baqarah (Chapter 2) is the longest surah with 286 verses.

questions.text: In Islamic jurisprudence, what is "Ijma"?
options: Scholarly consensus on a legal matter
The ruling of a single Caliph
questions.explanation: Ijma (إجماع) is the consensus of qualified Islamic scholars on a legal ruling. It is the third source of Islamic law after Quran and Sunnah.

questions.text: Which companion of the Prophet (SAW) is known as "The Trustworthy" (Al-Amin)?
questions.explanation: The Prophet Muhammad (SAW) himself was called Al-Amin (The Trustworthy) by the Quraysh before prophethood.

questions.text: What is "Laylat al-Qadr" (The Night of Power) better than?
questions.arabicText: ليلة القدر خير من؟
questions.explanation: Allah says in Surah Al-Qadr: "The Night of Power is better than a thousand months." (97:3)

questions.text: What is the ruling (hukm) on fasting on Eid al-Fitr?
questions.explanation: It is haram (forbidden) to fast on both Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha. These are days of celebration and eating.

questions.text: Which battle is referred to as "Yawm al-Furqan" (Day of Distinction) in the Quran?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Badr (624 CE) is called Yawm al-Furqan in Surah Al-Anfal. It was the first major battle of Islam.

questions.text: In the science of hadith, what is a "Hadith Mutawatir"?
options: A hadith narrated by one person only
A weak hadith with broken chain
A hadith narrated by so many people that fabrication is impossible
A hadith verified by Imam Bukhari alone
questions.explanation: A Hadith Mutawatir is narrated by such a large number of people at every level that it is considered impossible to fabricate.

questions.text: Which Prophet was thrown into the fire by Nimrod and emerged unharmed?
questions.arabicText: أي نبي ألقاه نمرود في النار وخرج سالماً؟
questions.explanation: Nimrod threw Prophet Ibrahim (AS) into a massive fire. Allah commanded the fire: "Be cool and safe for Ibrahim." (Quran 21:69)

questions.text: What is the meaning of "Taqwa"?
questions.arabicText: ما معنى "التقوى"؟
options: God-consciousness and piety — fearing Allah and obeying Him
questions.explanation: Taqwa is often translated as God-consciousness or piety — being aware of Allah in all your actions and striving to please Him.
